Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Miller: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. we have priya, our solutions engineer, too. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Alex Chen: good, thanks. i'm alex. we try to keep this tight, we have like 45 minutes. want to understand quickstart path and what tradeoffs we should be thinking about — hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:14] Marta Lopez: yes, and also, how quickly can we get to first token? we have a small demo for investors in two weeks so timeline matters.
[00:19] Priya Shah: absolutely. high level — hosted is fastest to get started, we give free credits and an API key so you can be up in hours. dedicated is reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput, and private gives the VPC/on-prem control for compliance.
[00:30] Samir Patel: quick question, when you say "free credits" — are there heavy rate limits or warmup penalties? our traffic spikes can be pretty bursty.
[00:37] Jordan Miller: great question. for PLG quickstarts we do throttle to protect the cluster but it's super generous for proofs — and you can request burst increases. the quickstart credit flow is designed to get you to a demo with realistic samples.
[00:48] Nina Rivera: also curious about log retention and audit, we have internal audit teams that ask for long term logs.
[00:52] Priya Shah: hosted has configurable retention tiers; for enterprise we can increase retention or export to your S3. for Private, audit logs stay in your VPC and you control retention via your infra.
[01:01] Alex Chen: ok, on security — do you support SSO/SAML? and KMS integration for key management?
[01:07] Jordan Miller: yes to both. SSO with SAML and SCIM for provisioning. KMS/HSM integrations are available for Dedicated and Private, hosted supports customer-managed keys via our KMS bridge for enterprise customers.
[01:18] Marta Lopez: and SOC2? we need attestation for vendor review.
[01:22] Priya Shah: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs — i'll drop the attestation and the security pack after the call.
[01:28] Alex Chen: lovely. now performance: our workload is short chat completions ~200 tokens with context, p95 latency needs to be sub-300ms for UX reasons, cost target is mid-range — we don't want premium GPU pricing if avoidable. can Redwood meet that on hosted?
[01:44] Priya Shah: p95 <300ms for 200 tokens is aggressive on some models, depends on model family. we have optimized kernels and prefix-KV caching to reduce latency, but the common pattern is: hosted lowest friction, Dedicated gives you tighter latency SLOs (reserved GPU pools), and Private removes network hops if on-prem.
[02:00] Samir Patel: what about the K-V cash? sorry, K-V cash? i saw that in docs — how does that affect latency?
[02:07] Priya Shah: haha, K-V cache — sometimes transcribed as cash — K-V cache stores key-value states of the attention cache so for multi-turn chat we avoid re-computing. it improves latency significantly for repeated context.
[02:18] Alex Chen: and what about cost optimization? we've looked at quantized runtimes and batching.
[02:23] Priya Shah: we recommend a mix: for latency-sensitive calls keep smaller batch sizes and lower quantization aggressiveness; for background embeddings or async tasks use higher batching and 4-bit quantization. Redwood Optimize will suggest batching configs and quant profiles based on your observed workload.
[02:36] Marta Lopez: if we start with hosted and then move to dedicated, how seamless is the routing and rollout?
[02:41] Jordan Miller: seamless — same API and model catalog. you can pin model versions and set rollout policies; traffic can be routed by latency or cost policy. also automatic fallback to compatible variants if capacity is constrained.
[02:52] Alex Chen: we might need private deployment later for EU data residency. what are typical lead times?
[02:57] Jordan Miller: for Private VPC it's usually 4–8 weeks depending on region and networking approvals; on-prem is longer because of air-gapped packaging, typically 8–12 weeks. Dedicated is faster — provisioning reserved pools in a couple of weeks once contract signed.
[03:12] Nina Rivera: what about encryption at rest and in transit?
[03:15] Priya Shah: TLS in transit, and encryption at rest with customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we can enable CMEK via our KMS bridge with customer keys.
[03:24] Samir Patel: curious about limits for streaming responses and function calling — we use tool calls a lot.
[03:29] Priya Shah: streaming is supported on hosted and Dedicated; function/tool calling patterns work the same. large streaming throughput benefits from Dedicated since you can reserve capacity to avoid preemption.
[03:39] Alex Chen: ok, let's talk pilot success criteria. what do you recommend?
[03:42] Jordan Miller: milestones: 1) TTFT — get to first token with your sample app within 48 hours using quickstart credits. 2) Perf baseline — Redwood SE runs a perf test against a realistic payload to measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens. 3) Integration checklist — SSO, logging, KMS validation. 4) Go/no-go criteria: p95 under target and cost within expected budget.
[04:03] Marta Lopez: sample app is react based, calls streaming chat for suggestions. maybe we can share the demo code.
[04:07] Priya Shah: perfect — if you share a sample request shape and concurrency, we can do a baseline.
[04:11] Alex Chen: our concurrency is unpredictable; typical baseline is 50 rps with spikes to 250 for short bursts.
[04:16] Priya Shah: that's helpful; we'll propose batching/caching configs. Dedicated autoscaling and burst capacity options can handle spikes better.
[04:25] Jordan Miller: one practical question — time-to-first-token for quickstart: usually under 2 hours if you follow the quickstart and we provide credits. that's accounts for API key, sample app wiring, and initial warmup.
[04:36] Samir Patel: two hours sounds good. any gotchas with rate limits that can block the investor demo?
[04:41] Jordan Miller: for demos we can bump limits for that timeframe. we'll include instructions on how to request a temporary increase in the quickstart docs.
[04:48] Nina Rivera: about billing — can we get a cost projection for expected traffic? we need to justify to finance.
[04:53] Jordan Miller: yes, i'll include a modeled run rate using your shared traffic profile. we'll show hosted vs dedicated unit economics so you can see break-even points.
[05:01] Alex Chen: one more — compliance: do you have an audit log export for SIEM integration (we use Splunk)?
[05:06] Priya Shah: yes, audit logs can be exported to your S3 or pushed to a SIEM endpoint for hosted enterprise; for Private it's native.
[05:13] Marta Lopez: ok great. thanks, this is helpful.
[05:16] Jordan Miller: to recap and close, we'll: send security pack and SOC2 attestation, issue a trial credit code and quickstart guide, and schedule an SE perf call next week to run baseline tests.
[05:27] Alex Chen: sounds good. we'll share sample request shapes and the demo code by Friday.
[05:31] Jordan Miller: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the notes and links.
